notes.text: The frozen target is מהואך; the provenance OCR had מתואך. The intended place-name remains unresolved.

The saved local V42 notice headed רב שמואל מתואך supplies a candidate comparison for the provenance מתואך; its body cites Niddah 33a and Bei Tu’akh. This internal comparison does not settle frozen מהואך or independently verify that folio. No place-name emendation or identity binding is made.

The consulted scan of Hyman, volume III, printed p. 1132, reads רב שמואל. ערך רב שמואל מתואך. The English retains the frozen מהואך rather than silently substituting the printed מתואך. In the directly consulted Niddah 33b passage, Rav Pappa arrives at לתואך and an elderly woman praises Rav Shmuel; the separately preserved Hyman notice instead cites 33a and writes בי תואך. These comparisons clarify the printed pointer without identifying a modern locality or establishing an authority identity. The earlier notes record the state before these printed-page and 33b inspections.
